title: ASER versus NAS/PARAKH: the central learning-measurement dispute
whatChanged: India has two national learning instruments that report incompatible pictures, and the official one has been reset three times in seven years. The pre-2017 NAS, NAS 2017, NAS 2021 and PARAKH Rashtriya Sarvekshan 2024 are four incompatible instruments wearing one name - different grades, frames, administrators and metrics - each of which its own custodians say breaks comparison with its predecessor, so there is no official national learning trend line at all. ASER, an NGO household survey, is the only continuous series. The headline contrast is stark: PARAKH 2024 reports Grade 3 language at 64 per cent and mathematics at 60, while ASER 2024 reports 27.1 per cent of Standard III children able to read a Standard II text and 33.7 per cent able to subtract.
bridgeNote: No linking study, no equating design and no anchor items exist between the two scales. ASER Centre states plainly that 'their results are not comparable'; nobody disputes it and nobody has built a bridge. What DOES reconcile, and is the most under-appreciated fact in the dispute, is that thresholding NAS's own data reproduces ASER: the World Bank applied a Minimum Proficiency Level benchmark to NAS 2017 Grade 5 data and found 54 per cent below it, against ASER 2018's 49.5 per cent of Standard V unable to read a Standard II text. Five points apart, same direction, same population. Most of the headline contradiction is a category error: a mean item-success rate is not a headcount ratio, and the two instruments broadly agree that about half of Indian children finish primary school unable to read at a Standard II level.

competingAccounts.position: Scale: 21.15 lakh students in 2024 and 34 lakh in 2021 against ASER's roughly 650,000, larger than almost any national assessment anywhere. It covers urban India, which ASER simply does not - and the gap is not trivial in PARAKH's own data, with urban leading rural by 7 points in Grade 9 language. It resolves school-management types ASER cannot, a limitation NAS's own critics concede. It covers grades ASER cannot: ASER applies the same floor tool to a 16-year-old as to a 6-year-old, and for secondary education NAS/PARAKH is the only national instrument that exists. It has diagnostic depth at item-cluster level and district actionability across 781 districts. And from 2021 the conflict-of-interest charge was answered structurally: CBSE as external administrator, external observers from unrelated schools, confidentiality agreements, tamper-evident OMR return bags, locked trunks and MoE-appointed validators - the very reform the academic critique asked for.

Independence from the body being graded: no budget, ranking, promotion or NIPUN Bharat target depends on ASER's number, whereas nothing in NAS/PARAKH's architecture makes the measurer independent of the measured - even the improved 2024 design has CBSE, a board under the Ministry, observing schools under the Ministry, on behalf of a ministry being evaluated, with execution running through the state education departments the survey grades. The household frame catches whom the school frame structurally cannot, and the exclusion is written into the sampling protocol. Oral one-on-one administration is the only format that yields information about a non-reader: PARAKH's Grade 3 items are four-option multiple choice and the Guidelines instruct that students read the passage silently by themselves, so a Grade 3 non-reader contributes a 25 per cent guess rather than a zero. And the method has not changed since 2006, against three official resets in seven years.

competingAccounts.holder: Johnson and Parrado (2021), the decisive independent finding
competingAccounts.position: 'NAS state averages are significantly higher than ASER state averages and averages from an independently conducted nationally representative survey. In addition, state rankings based on NAS data display almost no correlation with state rankings based on ASER, IHDS, or net state domestic product per capita. We conclude that NAS state averages are likely artificially high and contain little information about states' relative performance.' The correlations: ASER to IHDS +0.62, NAS to ASER +0.19, NAS to IHDS -0.03, NAS to state income +0.05, against a benchmark of +0.82 for ASER reading to ASER maths on the same children. This is the layer that survives every correction, because frame differences shift levels roughly in common across states and rankings are exactly where they wash out. They also foreclose the innocent explanations: the tested-level difference runs the wrong way, and voluntary absence has a very small effect. Their recommendation is to 'avoid use of NAS altogether' - and they warn that NITI Aayog's School Education Quality Index rests largely on NAS data, which makes SEQI a contaminated composite that must not be used as evidence of learning anywhere.

competingAccounts.holder: The mechanism, demonstrated experimentally in India (Singh 2020/2024)
competingAccounts.position: In Madhya Pradesh's Pratibha Parv, comparing responses to the same questions by the same students in the administrative test versus an independent test shows a DOUBLING of reported achievement, worst among low-performing students. In an Andhra Pradesh randomised experiment across more than 2,400 schools, paper-based assessments proctored by teachers severely exaggerate achievement in both private and government schools - roughly 20 per cent - with no such distortion in tablet-based assessments. Singh did not test NAS. But NAS 2017 was a paper-based, group-administered, in-school assessment - exactly the modality shown to distort - and the distortion is worst for low performers, precisely the shape needed to produce 'high everywhere and uninformative about relative performance'. This layer stands unrebutted for 2017 and 2021 and is simply untested for 2024.

competingAccounts.holder: The critique that runs the other way
competingAccounts.position: ASER is not clean either, and by the same authors. A Kane-Staiger variance decomposition finds 5-9 per cent of the variance in state score LEVELS is transitory - state levels are solid - but a third to a half of the variance in CHANGES in state scores and over 75 per cent of the variance in changes in district scores is transitory, and the noise is non-sampling, attributed to volunteer surveyors and the right-hand-rule household walk in place of a full listing. Separately, Joshi (2024) shows against an external benchmark that pre-2011 ASER estimates are systematically biased upwards, with the bias disappearing after robust survey procedures were introduced in 2011 - so a record attributing a learning collapse to the UPA on ASER evidence would be overclaiming, though Joshi's conclusion is that the real decline was smaller than previously thought, not zero.

notes:
Operative rules for this instrument, in order. On TRENDS: build the spine on ASER, from 2011-12 onward - it is the only continuous series and NAS/PARAKH cannot carry a trend by its own custodians' admission. On LEVELS: carry both and never difference them, noting the World Bank convergence as the honest reconciliation. On INTER-STATE comparison: use ASER levels, not NAS; do not use SEQI at all. On SECONDARY education: there is no independent instrument, so Grade 9 mathematics at 37 per cent raw or 16 points above chance carries a wide band and an explicit note that no second source exists. On ASER DELTAS below the national level: caveat or omit.

THE VERDICT ON THE DISPUTE ITSELF is roughly two-thirds different facts and one-third different weightings, in four separable layers. Layer 1, the largest, is a category error - mean against headcount - and is manufactured. Layer 2 is genuinely different populations, each measurable and each with a documented direction; note that the single most obvious explanation, ASER testing a floor two to four grades below, predicts ASER should read HIGHER, and it does not, which is why frame differences cannot close the gap on their own. Layer 3 is instrument integrity and is where the dispute is real. Layer 4 is a values question about what a national learning number should mean, and both answers are defensible.

A FINDING ABOUT THIS INSTRUMENT'S OWN TIER LADDER, recorded because it is not a data problem: by the letter of the tier definition ASER is T4, the same grade as a newspaper report, because it is an NGO dataset - while PARAKH 2024, whose National Report contains no methodology section and whose 274 MB 'Technical Report' is a rasterised image file with no extractable psychometrics, is T1 because it is official. Every ASER series in this drop is graded T4 as the schema requires and carries the anomaly in its caveat. This is the sort of thing the tier description's own rule - grade what you hold, not what it is about - was written to prevent in the opposite direction.

The bands INVERT against the means - language has the higher mean (64) but the lower proficiency share (57), mathematics the lower mean (60) but the higher share (65) - which can only happen if the two subjects' cut-scores sit at different points of their distributions. That inversion is itself the proof that the missing information is load-bearing rather than technical.

title: UDISE+ moves to individual student records: the 2022-23 reporting-base shift
whatChanged: From reference year 2022-23 UDISE+ collects individual student-level records with a portal-generated unique educational ID and voluntary Aadhaar, replacing school-wise consolidated returns, with the stated purpose of 'weeding out of duplicate or ghost entries'. Total enrolment fell from 26.52 crore (FY2021-22) to 25.18 crore (FY2022-23) to 24.80 crore (FY2023-24). The Ministry's own disclaimer states data from 2022-23 'is not strictly comparable with the previous reports on various educational indicators such as GER, NER, Dropout rate etc.' In the SAME breath the disclaimer discloses that the denominator moved too: population projections were 'moderated' by the Ministry using SRS birth-rate trends, UIDAI Aadhaar-saturation reports and the trends of adjoining states - so numerator and denominator were re-based in the same year.
bridgeNote: No back-cast, no dual-basis year and no reconciliation table appears in any UDISE+ report retrieved. The Ministry's position is purely declarative: pre-2021-22 and post-2022-23 are two series and may not be joined. There is no published estimate of how much of the fall is deduplication and how much is real decline - the one quantity that would let anyone close the ledger. The Ministry holds both bases and could produce a dual run for one year, so this is a non-publication rather than an impossibility.
competingAccounts: The Ministry's account is that the reform is an improvement in data quality: individual records with unique IDs permit dropout tracking and prevent duplicate or ghost beneficiaries claiming Samagra Shiksha, PM POSHAN and scholarship entitlements. Deduplication can only remove records, never add them, so a fall in the count is what a successful clean-up looks like.

The sceptical account is threefold. First, the intensity of the correction maps administrative capacity rather than schooling: Aadhaar seeding reached only 79.4 per cent nationally in 2023-24, ranging from Meghalaya 24.2 and Bihar 38.8 to Andhra Pradesh 98.1, so the measured fall is larger where Aadhaar penetration is higher, which has nothing to do with children. Second, the fall is concentrated in primary - a 14.4 per cent fall in Classes I-V in two years against a roughly flat higher secondary - and a pure-deduplication story has to explain why ghosts were so concentrated there; it is plausible, since mid-day-meal and scholarship incentives attach most strongly to primary, but the Ministry has never evidenced it. Third, Aadhaar appears on BOTH sides of the GER ratio - the numerator deduplicated using it, the denominator moderated using UIDAI saturation reports - which is a genuine circularity.

On the disclosure itself: the break was disclosed, but the disclosure was constructed after the fact. The 2022-23 report carries the incomparability language in a weaker form, with no bridge sentence and no mention of the population-projection moderation; the explicit claim that '2022-23 and 2023-24 are comparable' appears only retrospectively, in the 2023-24 report. The two reports were released together, end-December 2024, so the break-year datum entered the public record already paired with a successor, which structurally discourages anyone from treating 2022-23 as the break year.

title: The 2025-26 NEP structural reclassification and its contradicting back-cast
whatChanged: From 2025-26 UDISE+ reclassifies the school ecosystem into the NEP 5+3+3+4 stages - Foundational, Preparatory, Middle, Secondary - from the 10+2 structure, and re-casts every education indicator with it. bridgeNote: The two structures are not alternative presentations of one quantity. Foundational spans pre-primary through Class II while Primary spans Classes I-V; Preparatory (III-V) reads 95.4 for FY2024-25 against 90.9 for Classes I-V. Any series built here must be tagged by STRUCTURE as well as by year, and the two must never be spliced. The same problem applies to PTR, which is published simultaneously on both structures - Foundational 10 and Primary 20 for adjacent years describe different populations.

title: Pupil-teacher ratio: two breaks on opposite sides of the ratio, and PTR is not named in the disclaimer
whatChanged: PTR's numerator is enrolment, the quantity re-based to individual student records in 2022-23; its denominator is teachers, into which guest and part-time teachers were admitted for the first time in 2023-24. Both re-basings push PTR down spuriously, in consecutive years, on opposite sides of the ratio. The formula, the denominator construction and the double-counting convention are identical either side of the break - which is precisely why the enrolment shock transmits at full strength: nothing was fixed to absorb it. And in all four editions retrieved the Ministry's incomparability disclaimer names exactly three indicators - GER, NER and dropout rate - and never names PTR, the one headline indicator whose numerator is the raw re-based enrolment count itself.
bridgeNote: There is no continuous national PTR series spanning FY2021-22 to FY2023-24; treat the series as two segments and never splice. The pre-break series is solid and reproducible - an independent researcher working from UDISE+ 2021-22 microdata reproduces the Ministry's published level-wise PTR exactly (26 / 19 / 18 / 27) - so it is only across the break that the series fails. The break-year fall itself decomposes: holding teachers fixed at FY2021-22 and applying the new enrolment gives 24.15 against a published 23.30, so 70 per cent of the movement is the enrolment re-basing alone. Roughly seven-tenths of the celebrated improvement in primary PTR in the break year is children being deleted from a database - a child removed as a duplicate was never in the classroom, and removing them improves the measured ratio without a teacher being appointed or a child being taught differently.
competingAccounts: A third, smaller and entirely undocumented discontinuity sits inside the denominator. At the break the total teacher headcount barely moved (-0.25 per cent) while the sum of the four level-teacher counts rose 1.76 per cent: teacher deduplication did not shrink the headcount, what changed was how teachers were reported across levels, with proportionally more recorded as spanning multiple levels. Because a multi-level teacher is counted in full at every level they touch, this inflates every level denominator and depresses every level PTR independently of the enrolment effect. No UDISE+ report discusses it.

The guest-teacher coverage change is stated in exactly one place - a footnote in a research paper, not in any ministry document: 'UDISE 2021-22 does not include guest teachers, i.e. teachers who are on an ad-hoc appointment against a substantive post; this option is available along with part-time teachers from the 2023-24 cycle onwards. These numbers are not easily available but could be up to 10 to 15 per cent of the government and government-other workforce deployed in a state.' The published counts are consistent with it - 94,83,294 (2022-23) to 98,07,600 (2023-24), the largest single-year rise in the series, in exactly that year - but consistency is not proof, since genuine recruitment would look the same. The consequence either way is that pre-2023-24 teacher totals undercount people actually teaching by an unknown amount.

A THIRD break, in the UPA period, for anyone building back to the baseline. DISE restated its own level-wise PTR denominators at the 2012-13/2013-14 edition boundary, footnoting the exclusion of secondary and higher-secondary teachers in composite schools: the 2012-13 upper-primary PTR was restated from 25 to 18, a 28 per cent revision, by changing the denominator alone. Three official values therefore circulate for 2012-13 primary PTR - 34.0 from the UDISE+ back-chart, 28 from contemporaneous DISE and 27 from restated DISE - and the basis of the 34.0 could not be established, so it is carried nowhere in this instrument.

title: Teacher vacancies: two irreconcilable official aggregates and an undefined sanctioned-post base
whatChanged: The Ministry of Education has never established and does not maintain a national teacher-vacancy statistic. For 2023-24 they differ by 1,12,501 posts: 8,46,647 against 9,59,148, with secondary sanctioned strength differing by 6,01,224. The Department told the Committee in writing that vacancy data 'are maintained by the respective State governments/Union Territory administrations', and the Committee had to recommend in 2025 that it 'seek data from the State/UT Governments and maintain it centrally'. The Department did not accept the recommendation.
when: 2021-22 onward; Committee exchanges March 2025 and March 2026
bridgeNote: The most likely mechanism for the 2023-24 divergence is that 'Secondary' in the Committee-furnished aggregate absorbs higher secondary while the PAB aggregate's does not, plus Tamil Nadu's re-inclusion - but NEITHER DOCUMENT DEFINES ITS LEVELS, so that is inference, not established fact. competingAccounts.position: Education is in the Concurrent List; an overwhelming majority of schools are under the administrative control of States and UTs; recruitment, service conditions and rational deployment come under state governments; and recruitment is a continuous process as vacancies keep arising through retirement, resignation and new schools. competingAccounts.holder: Rajya Sabha Standing Committee on Education
competingAccounts.position: 'Since the funds under SSA are granted to State/UT Governments by the Union Government, it is imperative for the Department of School Education and Literacy to seek data from the State/UT Governments and maintain it centrally.' competingAccounts: On the portal the Department points to: as at 2026-08-02 prabandh.education.gov.in does not resolve in DNS from two independent network paths. Wayback holds captures from January 2024 to June 2025 and the archived landing page renders only its title and a JavaScript notice. It is a Samagra Shiksha planning and appraisal MIS for state officials, not a public statistics product; no public dashboard, download or report of teacher vacancies was ever exposed on it on the evidence of the archive. So the position is that the Department declines to maintain the statistic, points to a portal as where the data goes, and the portal is a login-gated administrative system that is currently unreachable.

On the quality of what does circulate: in the PAB annexure 'Vacant' is not measured but derived, equal to sanctioned minus in-position in every state row; Uttar Pradesh's elementary row is byte-identical for two consecutive years; six states report exactly zero elementary vacancies in 2023-24; the 2023-24 total silently excludes Tamil Nadu with no footnote, so the printed Total row sums a different set of states in the third column than in the first two; and Karnataka's 2021-22 elementary row implies a 71.8 per cent vacancy rate followed by a tripling of the teaching force in one year, meaning the national 2021-22 figure contains roughly a lakh posts that are a reporting error.

The same non-answer covers contract status. title: Education spending has two official numerators and they move in opposite directions
whatChanged: The Ministry of Education publishes two totals for public education spending side by side, in one table, for the same year: education departments only, and education and other departments. For FY2021-22 they are 2.75 and 4.12 per cent of GDP - a gap of 1.37 percentage points, with the narrow figure two-thirds of the headline. The choice of numerator reverses the direction of the last decade. On the broad basis FY2013-14 to FY2021-22 runs 3.84 to 4.12 per cent, an improvement; on the narrow basis it runs 2.97 to 2.75, a decline. Same budgets, opposite direction, purely from numerator choice. 'India spends X per cent of GDP on education' has no single true answer.
bridgeNote: The two are not convertible by a constant and must never be treated as one series with an offset: across the twenty-two-year table the gap runs from 0.52 points (FY2004-05) to 1.46 (FY2016-17), roughly tripling, and other departments' share of the total rose from 15.9 per cent (2004-05) to 33.3 (2021-22). The decomposition IS available, which is why this is a definitional dispute rather than an unmeasurable one: the broad column can be resolved to ministry level from the ABE's own Statement 1.
competingAccounts: The broad total is the official headline and the one that carries authority. Parliament is briefed on it - the Standing Committee's 363rd Report reproduces the broad series verbatim, every value matching - and the 6 per cent commitment is invoked against it. Its rationale is that education spending booked by non-education ministries is real education spending: the government's own note lists medical and public health education, agriculture research and education, welfare of SC/ST/OBC and minority education, scientific research, education under social security, mid-day meal nutrition, police training and rural development training.

The narrow total is what most readers mean by education spending. The broad column includes TRAINING, which the narrow one excludes - 20,205 crore, 0.09 points of GDP, in FY2021-22 - so the two columns are not like-for-like. The Ministry of Education is 39 per cent of the Centre's own broad education spending of 1.02 per cent of GDP, and under a tenth of the 4.12 per cent all-India headline, which is Centre plus States; the top four non-education ministries alone come to 90 per cent of the entire Ministry of Education budget. And the ABE concedes the sector allocation is an assumption, not a measurement: the breakup of other departments' spending 'is not available in the budget documents' and is assigned on the stated ground that it mainly goes to elementary and secondary education.

The consequence for the 6 per cent target is that the gap to it is 1.9 points or 3.3 points depending on a definitional choice that is never stated when the target is invoked. Two further sharpeners: the ABE never mentions the 6 per cent target, NEP 2020 or Kothari in any edition, so the comparison is made outside the statistical document; and Kothari's '6 per cent of national income' was not verified against the original, which matters because national income is a smaller denominator than GDP at market prices, so the Kothari 6 per cent and the NEP 6 per cent may not be the same bar.

title: The education budget analysis stopped being published, and its last two points are estimates
whatChanged: The Analysis of Budgeted Expenditure on Education, an annual Ministry of Education publication running since at least 2000-01, has published no edition covering FY2022-23 or later. The series terminates at FY2021-22, a four-year gap in a twenty-five-year annual statistical series, and T3 has zero observations. Separately, the terminal points of both spending series are Budget Estimates, which are systematically revised down: on the only year where all three stages exist, the broad basis reads BE 4.39, RE 4.30, Actual 4.04 - a 0.35-point BE-to-Actual revision. The last Actual on either series is FY2019-20.
when: FY2022-23 onward; the last edition is dated 2024 and covers to FY2021-22
bridgeNote: Two things cannot be recovered. First, the estimate stage of rows FY2000-01 to FY2018-19 is INFERRED from publication convention - in every edition the last three rows are Actual, Revised Estimate and Budget Estimate and all earlier rows are Actuals - and is not annotated in the source for those years. Second, the schema has no field for estimate stage and cannot express it: `status` is an evidence grade (verified/approx/pending) and stage is orthogonal to it, since a Budget Estimate can be perfectly verified and still be wrong by 0.3 points. Until a field exists, stage is carried in each point's note and must render.
competingAccounts: Whether the publication lapsed or merely became unreachable is not settled. Both research passes established that education.gov.in now serves a client-rendered application returning HTTP 200 with an empty shell for any path - verified with five fabricated ABE paths, all returning 200 with no content - and a Wayback CDX check establishes that nothing newer than the 2024 edition was ever archived. But neither queried the site's runtime API nor retrieved from an Indian IP, so the alternative - that an edition exists and is merely unlinked, making this link rot rather than a lapse in a twenty-five-year series - is not excluded. `not-published` is the right reasonKind on the evidence held, with that verification outstanding.

The corroborating evidence that Budget Estimates overstate comes from a completely different direction and agrees: the Union Ministry of Education underspent its own Budget Estimate in 13 of 16 completed years at a mean of 6.31 per cent, cumulatively 83,582 crore across FY2009-10 to FY2024-25. Economic Survey 2023-24 quoted 4.64 per cent - a Budget Estimate for a year whose Actual was never published - as 'latest available'.

title: AISHE: the GER denominator was restated, and the survey ceased to be timely
whatChanged: Two things happened to India's higher-education statistic. First, the denominator was restated: every GER published before the AISHE 2020-21 report rests on 2001-Census-based population projections and everything from 2020-21 onward rests on 2011-Census-based projections, which are about 6 per cent larger and mechanically cut GER by roughly 1.5 points. AISHE states it plainly - 25.6 for 2019-20 on the 2011 projection against 27.1 on the 2001 projection - so as-published and restated values for the same year differ by up to 1.5 points and cannot share a column. Second, the publication lag opened from under a year in the mid-2010s to 42 months for AISHE 2022-23, which appeared on 8 July 2026 alongside AISHE 2023-24, after a 29-month interval with no AISHE publication at all.
when: Denominator restatement in the 2020-21 report (published 29 January 2023); lag from 2019-20 onward
bridgeNote: The restatement bridges completely and AISHE published the bridge: a full 2011-basis series back to 2011-12 exists and reproduces the published GERs exactly against the published projections (4,46,32,261 divided by 151,161,000 gives 29.53). That restated series is what this instrument carries. The direction is uniform and known - every pre-2020-21 as-published figure is too high by roughly 1.5 points at 2019-20 levels - but the affected span runs from 2011-12 to 2019-20, straddling the political transition rather than sitting on one side of it, which is why the directional values of this field do not fit and `degrades-precision` is used with the direction stated here instead. One consequence worth naming: the year female GER crossed above male is itself basis-dependent, reading 2017-18 on the restated series and 2018-19 as published.
competingAccounts: The lag is not a collection problem and the report says so: 'The Survey was held between 18th November, 2022 till March, 2024.' Collection closed in March 2024 and the report appeared 28 months later, so the binding constraint sits between scrutiny and publication, not in the field. And the lag is era-shaped: AISHE 2015-16, 2016-17 and 2017-18 each carried a cover year one year after the survey year; the lag opened in T2 and reached its maximum in T3.

The consequence is demonstrated rather than inferred, which makes this the strongest form of a not-published finding. Economic Survey 2025-26 quoted an AISHE 2022-23 higher-education GER of 29.5 while the AISHE 2022-23 report was still unpublished, and the same Survey's statistical appendix - unable to cite an unpublished report - fell back on AISHE 2021-22 and printed 28.4. The number was in government hands and used in the government's flagship economic document months before the report containing it was released. Producibility is not merely inferred here; it is shown.

A separate and compounding problem is that the numerator is a voluntary self-reported administrative return. The Ministry's own words: 'Participation in AISHE is voluntary, and the data is self-reported by the HEIs via AISHE web portal.' The headline participation rate of more than 90 per cent is post-pooling, not actual response - universities 96.9 per cent, colleges 92.0, standalone institutions 69.1 - with non-responders' totals filled by repeating their latest available data, so roughly 31 per cent of standalone institutions in the 2023-24 figures carry data one to two years old. This is P-22's shape in higher education.

title: Literacy is asked, not tested - and four official instruments use four rules
whatChanged: India's literacy rate is a self-declaration. In the Census, NSS and PLFS the enumerator poses the question to a household informant, frequently about other members, and no reading or writing task is administered at any point: a literate person is a person someone said was literate. Four official instruments apply four different rules to the same word. Census, NSS and PLFS form one definitional family - can both read and write a simple message with understanding, age 7 plus - differing in sampling and coverage rather than concept. CAMS is the outlier inside the official family: for anyone ever enrolled in formal education, completing pre-primary or Class I is definitionally literacy and 'no test of the ability was performed'. NFHS-5 is the only official instrument administering any reading task, and only below Standard 9, with partial credit, on a restricted 15-49/15-54 frame.
when: Census 1951 onward; PLFS 2025 is the latest measurement
bridgeNote: The self-declaration gap has been measured twice, and both measurements point the same way. NFHS-3 (2004-05) ran both methods on the same respondents: 69 per cent self-reported against 63.4 per cent when required to read a test card, a 5.6-point gap. A 1991 Literacy Survey re-contact found over 10 per cent of below-primary-educated persons reported literate by informants were illiterate when individually contacted, and only 70 per cent of below-primary self-identified literates demonstrated both reading and writing with comprehension. 5.6 points is a floor, not a ceiling: NFHS's card test is one sentence with partial credit and is skipped entirely above Standard 9.
competingAccounts: Two further definitional traps sit inside the official numbers. Census 2011's FINAL literacy rate is 72.98 per cent, computed from the Registrar General's own Primary Census Abstract; 74.04 is the PROVISIONAL figure released on 31 March 2011, and it is what appears in ministry documents, international compendia and the press. No official communication foregrounds the revision. Nothing is concealed - the final figure has been public since 2013 - but for an instrument tracking what the state knows against what the state says, this is a clean example of the two diverging. Any series splicing provisional-2011 to a later survey embeds a spurious 1.06-point step. Separately, the AGE FRAME costs about 4.7 points: Census 2011 reads 74.04 at 7 plus and 69.30 at 15 plus, so the frame belongs in the field name.

The UNESCO Institute for Statistics series for India, which the World Bank passes through, is neither a model projection nor a carry-forward from Census 2011: it is a spliced patchwork of three different Indian surveys switching instrument between adjacent years - 76.32 (2022, PLFS), 81.70 (2023, CAMS), 78.16 (2024, back to PLFS). A 5.4-point rise followed by a 3.5-point fall is demographically impossible for a stock variable, so any trend drawn through UIS India literacy for 2018-2024 measures instrument turnover rather than learning. UIS's own recoding rule is not even a literacy question: those reporting any level of formal schooling are coded literate, which is an attainment question with the 'not literate' bucket inverted.

The concrete point, and it is the reason ASER must never share an axis with a literacy rate. Under self-declaration 81.1 per cent of Indians aged 7 plus are literate (PLFS 2025). Under an administered task 48.8 per cent of children in Standard V can read a Standard II text (ASER 2024). Under CAMS, completing Class I is literacy by definition, unasked. More than half of Standard V children cannot read a text pitched three grades below them - and every one of them, on reaching 15 with 'primary' recorded as attainment, is counted literate by PLFS's ladder, by CAMS's Case II rule, by UIS's recoding, and by the Census too if an informant says so. The Standard II reading task is a harder test than the national literacy statistic.

title: RTE section 12(1)(c): the official 'seats' figure is a lagged reimbursement headcount
whatChanged: There is no published national series of seats notified against seats filled under the 25 per cent private-school quota, and the Government of India does not maintain one. What the Ministry publishes is a cumulative count of children in schools for which reimbursement is claimed, with no seats denominator. Worse, where the Ministry does use the word 'seats' the figure is demonstrably something else: for Karnataka, the 'total number of seats' for year Y equals exactly the Project Approval Board approved reimbursement headcount for year Y minus 1, for three consecutive years - which is why seats equalled admissions perfectly for 2021-22, 2022-23 and 2023-24, a hundred per cent fill rate by construction rather than by achievement. The apparent 19.1 per cent fill in 2024-25 is the artefact breaking down, not a sudden collapse.
when: 2012-13 onward; the Karnataka reply is dated 27 July 2026
bridgeNote: The only genuine national seats-versus-filled measurement ever made was a DISE-based exercise for 2012-13 and 2013-14: fill rates of 21.5 and 29.0 per cent, on about 21.1 lakh seats available and 6.1 lakh filled, with Rajasthan and Madhya Pradesh alone accounting for 320,000 of the 610,000. That it was constructible then is the point: this is a not-published problem sitting on top of a never-defined one, not an impossibility. Operative rule: any figure the Government of India labels 'seats' under section 12(1)(c) should be treated as a reimbursement-claim headcount until proven otherwise, and no national fill-rate series may be built on Ministry data.
competingAccounts: Two official-derived national series diverge by up to 1.95 million children in the same year, and both claim to come from the same PRABANDH/PAB pipeline. The Ministry's Lok Sabha replies give 4,372,723 / 4,523,080 / 4,896,953 for 2019-20 to 2021-22; a compilation from state PAB minutes gives 3,604,082 / 3,473,922 / 2,950,342 for the same years. This is a live data-integrity problem, not a rounding difference. The compilation's own limitations section concedes that PAB minutes 'capture only the reimbursement information, which may include information spread across years, and thus may not be unique to a given year', and that its school-participation figures exceed 100 per cent of all private schools in two states - which cuts against it and in favour of neither.

Even where fill rates are published by third parties, the denominator is not applied consistently: the same report computes fill against seats for one state and against applications received for another in the same table, so a figure quoted as a fill rate from that source must be recomputed against a stated base. On a seats base one state's 2020-21 reads 14.2 per cent against a printed 56.66.

On money as against children, the same structural blindness: the Ministry states that 'the Central share is released to State/UTs based on approved funding pattern and not intervention wise', so the Centre does not know and cannot report how much money actually reached schools under the provision. Approval is not release and release is not payment to schools. The cumulative approval shortfall of 2,451.39 crore across FY2020-21 to FY2024-25 is therefore a floor on the gap, not a measure of what schools are owed.

title: The government's education statistics are reachable only through third-party archives
whatChanged: Over 2025-2026 the Ministry of Education's document corpus ceased to be retrievable from government hosts. education.gov.in migrated to a client-rendered application whose entire legacy /sites/upload_files/mhrd/files/ tree - annual reports, statistics, and the whole pre-2025 parliamentary-annexure corpus - now returns HTTP 404 on every path, while returning HTTP 200 with an empty shell for fabricated paths. Across three independent research passes the following did not resolve or did not serve: dsel.education.gov.in, udiseplus.gov.in, dashboard.udiseplus.gov.in, education.gov.in, indiacode.nic.in, pib.gov.in, prabandh.education.gov.in, mospi.gov.in, nas.gov.in, ncert.nic.in, eparlib.sansad.in, cag.gov.in and all its mirrors, cabsec.gov.in, and main.sci.gov.in. Every UDISE+ report, every DISE Flash Statistics edition, every edition of the education budget analysis, the National Education Policy text itself, and the 1968 and 1986 policies were reconstructed from Internet Archive captures or third-party mirrors.
bridgeNote: There is no substitute for the primary host and the archive is not one: Wayback returned HTTP 429 under sustained use, several captures are truncated at exactly 1,048,576 bytes, and at least one capture downloads as zero bytes from a corrupt record. Some of these failures are network-reachability artefacts of the retrieval environment rather than dead documents and are worth retrying from an Indian IP; the education.gov.in 404s are not, since they were verified against fabricated paths.
competingAccounts: This is not a finding about education and it does not assert intent. It is recorded because it conditions the TIER of everything above it: under the rule that tier grades the document actually retrieved and not the institution the subject belongs to, a government statistic reachable only through a third-party archive is still T1 when the archive serves the ministry's own PDF byte-for-byte, but an official figure known only through a press account or a mirror is T4 or T3. Several figures in this drop are graded down for exactly that reason - the PAB teacher-vacancy annexure at T3 because it came from a mirror, the NAS 2017 and 2021 rows at T4 because the hosts do not resolve, the UDISE+ 2025-26 figures at T3 because the edition was never retrieved.

Two consequences are already visible in this phase and will worsen. First, the newest edition of the education budget analysis ever archived is the 2024 one, so the archive cannot distinguish 'never published' from 'published and unlinked'. Second, the government's own statistical estimate of its school system is, at the time of writing, reachable only through a third-party archive - and the archive is a volunteer-funded American non-profit under no obligation to keep it.

title: MHA's headline J&K 'terrorist incidents' figure includes MHA's own operations
whatChanged: MHA publishes two incident quantities that are routinely both called incidents, and one is the sum of the other plus operations initiated by the security forces. From the Annual Report 2022-23 the J&K table carries 'Terrorist Initiated Incidents (TII)' and 'Encounters/Counter Terror operations' as separate columns; before it, and in the parliamentary reply of 20 July 2022, a single column headed 'Incidents' or 'Terrorist Incidents' carried their sum. The identity is exact on every year where both are available: 228+189=417 for 2018, 153+102=255 for 2019, 126+118=244 for 2020, 129+100=229 for 2021. Four years, four exact matches. The mechanism is stated once in the entire corpus, in Rajya Sabha Unstarred Question No. 210 of 12 December 2018: 'The number of incidents includes the violence committed by terrorists during anti militancy operations.' It never migrated into the series it describes, and neither column is defined anywhere in seventeen report years.
when: Composite basis to the Annual Report 2021-22 (posted 24 November 2022); components published separately from the Annual Report 2022-23 (posted 11 October 2023)
bridgeNote: Unusually for this phase, a bridge exists and is exact - but only from 2018. From the Annual Report 2022-23 onward MHA publishes both components, so the composite can be decomposed for 2018 to 2024 and the decomposition can be checked against the composite as separately published. For every year before 2018 no decomposition exists and the bridge does not.

competingAccounts.position: The table is labelled, the rule was stated to Parliament in December 2018, and from the Annual Report 2022-23 the components are published separately. 'Incidents of terrorist violence' has conventionally included encounters because an encounter is an incident of terrorist violence - the militants are present and armed in both cases, and the violence committed by them during an anti-militancy operation is violence.

An operation the state chooses to launch is not an event that happened to the state. Combining them makes the series respond to policy and operational tempo as much as to threat: an intensified year raises a number the government elsewhere wants low. The reply of 20 July 2022 uses the composite to make exactly the claim it cannot support - 'There has been substantial decline in terrorist attacks from 417 in 2018 to 229 in 2021' - when roughly 45 per cent of the 2018 figure is counter-terrorism operations conducted by the state. This position is available without disputing a single MHA number.

title: MHA restated the J&K incident series for 2017-2019 and never said why
whatChanged: The same column name, the same ministry, and two reports one year apart carry different values: 2017 falls from 342 to 279, 2018 from 614 to 417, 2019 from 594 to 255, while 2020 is unchanged at 244. No footnote, note or explanatory sentence accompanies the restatement in either report - the surrounding paragraphs of both were read and there is nothing. Both tables carry the identical heading structure and the identical introductory sentence form. And the Annual Report 2021-22 does not restate 2014, 2015 or 2016: it drops them, starting its window at 2017, so 222, 208 and 322 stand unrevised on the old basis while 2017 onward stands on the new one, and anyone assembling a 2014-2024 series from the Annual Reports splices two incompatible bases between 2016 and 2017 with nothing on the page to warn them. The seam is invisible because it falls in a gap rather than at a restated value.
bridgeNote: No MHA document reconciles the two bases. The 2020 figure is identical across both while 2018 falls by 197 and 2019 by 339, which rules out a uniform rescaling and points to a category being removed that was large in 2018-19 and negligible in 2020. The obvious candidate - law-and-order and stone-pelting events - is ruled out by MHA's own later reply, since organised stone-pelting alone was 1,328 in 2018 against a total of 614. What the removed events were is unestablished.

competingAccounts.holder: The case for the restated series
competingAccounts.position: The restated figures are the ministry's current published position and are consistent with the decomposed basis introduced one report later, which makes them the auditable series. A ministry that lowered its own count for 2018 and 2019 by 197 and 339 moved those years in the direction that makes its own record for them look worse, not better.

The restated series is the one that supports the decline narrative most strongly, and the years cut hardest are 2018 and 2019 - the years immediately before and including the abrogation of Article 370. The pre-restatement figures are not obviously wrong; they are simply no longer published, and no direction of error can be shown in either direction. Dropping them in favour of the later basis is the instrument silently adopting the state's own revision.

title: 'Civilians killed' means two different things in two MHA instruments, and changed meaning mid-series
whatChanged: For the same years MHA has published two civilian-death series under the same column name. On the bounded basis, Rajya Sabha Unstarred Question No. 371 of 20 July 2022 introduces its table as 'The number of security forces and civilians who died due to terrorist attacks since 2018', giving 39, 39, 37 and 41 for 2018 to 2021. On the composite basis, from the Annual Report 2022-23, the same years read 55, 44, 38 and 41, and the Annual Report 2023-24 footnote states: 'Civilians killed includes civilians killed in terrorist-initiated incidents and civilians killed in encounter/counter Terrorism operations.' The composite basis was introduced in the report posted 11 October 2023 without the footnote; the footnote first appears in the report posted 27 December 2024. For roughly fourteen months MHA published a redefined civilian-death series under an unchanged column name with no notice of the change, and the gap is dateable to the day at both ends.
when: Redefinition in the Annual Report 2022-23, posted 11 October 2023; disclosure in the Annual Report 2023-24, posted 27 December 2024
bridgeNote: The arithmetic residual between the two bases - 16 for 2018, 5 for 2019, 1 for 2020, 0 for 2021 - is NOT a bridge and must not be published as the count of civilians killed in security-force operations. Two reasons, both dispositive. The 2021 residual is zero, which would mean no civilian died in any encounter or counter-terrorism operation in J&K in that year, a claim no document makes. And the security-force-killed figure for 2020 also moved across the same restatement, from 62 to 63, which cannot be a civilian-definition effect - so the restatement carries ordinary revisions as well as the definitional change. The residual is a derived quantity whose basis is unestablished, and this is a hard stop.

competingAccounts.position: The composite is disclosed in the footnote and is a complete count of civilian deaths connected to the conflict, which is more informative than a count restricted to a single perpetrator. The revision moved the published civilian toll upward, which is the direction that makes the government's own record look worse, and PIB carried the same definition inside a row label ten months before the Annual Report footnote.

A count that names no perpetrator cannot answer the question the count exists to answer, and the disclosure arrived fourteen months after the redefinition. The broadened basis also reaches only deaths in encounters and counter-terrorism operations, so protest firing, crowd control, checkpoints and crowd-control munitions remain outside it - deaths MHA's own reports narrate in prose on the same pages as the tables that omit them.

title: The bounding sentence sits where transcription does not reach: six civilian deaths recorded to 31 July 2016
whatChanged: MHA has bounded 'Civilians killed' three different ways across its instruments, and in every case the bounding sits in surrounding prose rather than in the column heading. A bare label with no bounding at all appears in every Annual Report from 2008-09 to 2022-23; 'who died due to terrorist attacks' in the reply of 20 July 2022; and 'in these incidents' in the reply of 10 August 2016, whose annexure gives 163 incidents, six civilians killed and twelve civilians injured for 2016 up to 31 July. That answer was given five weeks into the unrest following the killing of Burhan Wani on 8 July 2016, during which large numbers of civilians were killed in security-force firing on protesters and the state's own later count puts pellet injuries alone in the thousands. The Annual Report 2016-17 later put the full year at 15 and recorded an 11.76 per cent decrease in casualties of civilians compared with 2015.
when: 10 August 2016; the pattern runs across MHA instruments from 2008-09 to 2024-25
bridgeNote: No bridge, and none is proposed here. The civilian death toll of the 2016 unrest is not established in this phase from any primary document, and MHA's figure must not be paired with any specific counter-figure whose own basis has not been established. competingAccounts.position: The answer is accurate to the question asked and states its scope on its face: Parliament asked about terrorist incidents, the annexure introduces itself as counting persons killed or injured in those incidents, and six is correct on that basis. The Annual Report's 11.76 per cent comparison is a like-for-like comparison of the same bounded series year on year, which is the only comparison that series supports.

The bound is stated in the one part of the document that does not survive use. Every chart, aggregator and press account built from these tables carries away the heading and discards the sentence, and MHA has never issued the figure with the bound attached to the label. The mechanism is reproducible: the widely-circulated compilations of MHA J&K data all carry the column name and not the sentence. The result is that the deadliest year for civilians in the period is recorded by the responsible ministry as an improvement for civilians, because the deaths it does not count are the ones the state caused.

title: Five 'incident' counts for one year, and the most-cited independent counter publishes no methodology
whatChanged: For calendar 2018 in Jammu and Kashmir, five separately published and separately labelled incident counts exist, all retrievable: 614 as 'Incidents' in the MHA Annual Reports 2018-19 to 2020-21; 597 as 'Number of Terrorism Related Incidents' from SATP; 417 as 'Terrorist Incidents' in MHA's reply of 20 July 2022; 228 as 'Terrorist Initiated Incidents' from the Annual Report 2022-23 onward; and 206 as 'Incidents of Killing' on SATP's fatalities datasheet. These are not measurement noise. 'Incidents of Killing' gates on a death; 'Terrorist Initiated Incidents' gates on who initiated; 'Terrorist Incidents' drops the initiation requirement; 'Incidents' is the widest official category; and 'Number of Terrorism Related Incidents' gates on a relation rather than an act and carries no published definition whatsoever. The near-coincidence of 228 and 206 is arithmetic accident - one filters on initiator, the other on outcome - and must not be treated as corroboration.
when: Concurrent, calendar 2018; the structural divergence runs throughout the period
bridgeNote: No bridge exists and none can, because one side of the comparison has no stated definition. The deeper structural point is that the two families of instrument fail in opposite directions: SATP gates on press reportability and misses routine, undramatic, remote-sector and communications-blackout events, while MHA gates on administrative reportability - an incident is what a police station and the UT administration book and forward - and misses events the state has an interest in not booking, and can re-book one operation as several. Neither is a superset of the other and no reconciliation exists.
competingAccounts: The South Asia Terrorism Portal publishes no methodology page, codebook, definitions page or inclusion criteria; its site structure was enumerated and none exists. Its entire methodology statement is a datasheet footer reading 'Compiled from news reports and are provisional'. Its own disclaimer nonetheless concedes that the data rests on 'publicly available information, internally developed data and other sources believed to be reliable' and that it does not guarantee accuracy, adequacy or completeness - so it asserts a non-press component without ever specifying what it is or which figures it touches. Its stated institutional purpose is to counter what it calls progressive distortions regarding terrorist movements in South Asia. It maintains MHA's figures as a separate 'Official Data' object, frozen at 2018 and reproducing the old MHA series, and no text on any reachable page acknowledges, compares or explains the gap between its own J&K civilian count and MHA's - a gap that for 2018 is 86 against 39 on the bounded basis and 55 on the composite.

MHA publishes no definition of 'Incidents', 'Terrorist Initiated Incidents' or 'Encounters/CT Ops.' in any of seventeen report years, and no MHA document states whether a fatality is required or whether firing, grenade attacks, IED recoveries and non-fatal attacks are inside the count. The one partial definitional sentence in the corpus is in a parliamentary answer of December 2018 and never migrated into the series. So on the fatality gate, SATP's 'Incidents of Killing' states its requirement on the face of the column and MHA states nothing at all - which means every comparison between the two is a comparison in which one side's definition is unknown and the other's is absent.

title: Infiltration: attempts, successful and net estimated are three quantities under overlapping labels, and the table was deleted
whatChanged: MHA's infiltration row label changed four times and then the table disappeared. It ran as an unlabelled 'Total' from at least 2010-11 to 2013-14; as 'Total Infiltration Attempts' with the attribution '(Source MAC)' in 2014-15; with an added 'Successful' row in 2015-16; as 'Net infiltration (Estimated)' in 2016-17; and as 'Net Estimated infiltration' from 2017-18 to 2022-23. MHA has never stated whether 'Successful' and 'net estimated' are the same quantity, and nowhere states how an infiltration attempt is detected or counted. The Annual Reports 2023-24 and 2024-25 contain no infiltration figures at all, while retaining the policy paragraph describing the multi-pronged approach to containing cross-border infiltration - the sentence about managing infiltration outlived the measurement of it by two report years and counting. The discontinuation was not announced. Net estimated infiltration for 2019 was separately restated from 138 to 141 in the Annual Report 2022-23 with no note.
when: Label changes across Annual Reports 2014-15 to 2017-18; restatement in 2022-23; series discontinued after the Annual Report 2022-23
bridgeNote: No bridge exists between attempts and net estimated infiltration, because MHA publishes no interception or attrition figure that would link them. The Ministry of Defence's 'Infiltration Bid Eliminated' cannot supply it either: it is scoped to the Line of Control under Army operational control and is therefore neither the same geography nor the same agency. A naive series built by taking whichever body published a figure in a given year is guaranteed to be wrong, because the three quantities move in opposite directions under one underlying reality - if interception improves, attempts may be unchanged, bids eliminated rise and net falls.

competingAccounts.position: One row is labelled an estimate on its face and the other is not, so the two are distinguished for any reader. Border management is operational rather than statistical, and the policy description of how infiltration is contained remains in the report in full detail while Parliament remains available to anyone who wants year-wise numbers.

A series published for more than a decade was withdrawn with no announcement and no reason, in the two reports immediately after the lowest figure it ever carried. Nothing marks the discontinuation on the page, and the reports also shortened the table's window twice - the 2021-22 and 2022-23 reports start at 2017 and drop 2014 to 2016 from view rather than restating them, so a reader of the current report cannot see infiltration at all and a reader of the 2022-23 report cannot see 2014 to 2016. title: A cumulative J&K death ledger that ran for three decades, then stopped, and never counted militants

When the ministry compressed the conflict into one sentence it dropped a third of it. title: MHA's J&K figures are produced by the CID of the J&K Police and published without attribution

title: 'Injured by pellets' is at least five different objects and no two instruments count the same one

Four collisions are established, each between a retrieved and a relayed rendering. 54 is the number of persons paid Rs 0.75 lakh for permanent disablement under government orders of 5 January and 26 February 2018 (retrieved, via the High Court judgment) and also the number said to have suffered some form of visual impairment in press renderings of the assembly reply (relayed). 510 is the number of patients referred to other hospitals in the country on the Director of Health Services' affidavit (retrieved) and also the number said to have been hospitalised out of 782 with eye injuries in press renderings of the assembly reply (relayed). 1,725 and 1,726 appear as the J&K government's rehabilitation list and as the SHRC's count of persons injured by metal pellets in 2016. And 782 and 728 are two press renderings of the same assembly reply's eye-injury figure, one of which is a transposition and it cannot be established which - so neither figure should be authored. No assertion is made here that any pair is the same underlying figure; the assertion is that they are used as though they were.

The most-quoted composite is the least establishable. It is the most-circulated pellet-injury number in existence and its basis cannot be established from anything retrieved in this phase. title: 'Blinded' has no official definition, and the only definitions that exist come from clinical work that disagrees with itself
whatChanged: Three thresholds, three shares, one hospital, overlapping populations. 'Completely blinded', defined as no perception of light, covers 10.8 per cent of 664 eyes in the prospective SMHS series. 'Visual impairment of varying degrees' covers 59.3 per cent of the same 664 eyes. 'Final best-corrected visual acuity of counting fingers or worse' covers 82.4 per cent of eyes in the 777-patient series. These are not inconsistent findings; they are three different questions. Meanwhile the state's vocabulary has no threshold at all: 'permanent disablement' and 'partial disablement' in Government Order No.61-Home of 2017, and 'visual impairment' in press renderings of the assembly reply, appear with no criterion, no examining authority and no acuity band anywhere. The public claim in this subject is mass blinding, and the number attached to it varies between roughly 54 and roughly 200 depending on which unstated threshold is implied.
bridgeNote: The clinical thresholds could in principle be mapped onto each other, since each states an acuity criterion. The administrative ones cannot, because they are not defined at all - so no bridge exists between any government figure and any clinical one.
competingAccounts: A figure for blindings is not a measurement of an uncertain quantity; it is a choice of threshold that nobody has disclosed. The inversion worth recording is that the clinical figures are the only ones with stated definitions and they are the least often quoted, while the government figures, which have no stated definition at all, are the ones that carry administrative consequences - who was paid and how much.

The absence is not a case of never-defined in the strict sense as regards the quantity itself: operable definitions exist and are in use in peer-reviewed clinical work on this very population, so a threshold could be adopted tomorrow and the count then collected. What meets never-defined is the narrower object - an official definition of blinding. On that, none has ever existed in any government instrument.

title: MHA counts pellet deaths month by month and refuses pellet injuries in the same sentence

title: AFSPA is reported annually for the North East at district granularity and never once for J&K
whatChanged: The Armed Forces (Special Powers) (Jammu and Kashmir) Act 1990 is never named in any MHA Annual Report retrieved - 2013-14, 2017-18, 2018-19, 2020-21, 2022-23, 2023-24 and 2024-25 all return zero occurrences of the Act's name in any of its forms - and no disturbed-area statement for J&K appears in any of them. Over the same years AFSPA 1958 in the North East is reported annually, in detail, as a measurable achievement: the Annual Report 2024-25 states at para 2.39 that because of considerable improvement in the security situation the imposition of AFSPA 1958 has been significantly reduced and that as on 1 April 2025 it applies only in three districts and three police stations of another district in Arunachal Pradesh. competingAccounts: This is not a claim that MHA conceals AFSPA's application in J&K - it is widely known and is stated elsewhere. The finding is about the instrument: the flagship annual accounting treats the two theatres asymmetrically, in the theatre where the same ministry reports 731 counter-terror operations over seven years, and where section 7 of the 1990 Act is the provision governing whether any of those operations can be prosecuted.

Section 7 requires prior Central Government sanction to prosecute a member of the armed forces for anything done under the Act's powers. Since 1990 sanction has been sought in 50 J&K cases, refused in 47 and pending in 3, and never granted. The decision rule that produced that record is held by nobody on both ministries' own account: the CPIO of the Ministry of Defence answered that the information is not in his custody and should be treated as nil, the Under Secretary (AG-I) that it is not maintained or available in his section, and the CPIO for the Indian Army that it is not available or held with the concerned agency of Headquarters. Both ministries denied custody of the same records, and the Central Information Commission then sealed the case files under section 8(1)(a) on 5 June 2020, reasoning that 'indisputably, the larger public interest of the State (vis-a-vis its susceptibility to unrest) prevails over that of the alleged victims.'

title: Custodial deaths: the unit of account is the State police, and the J&K series breaks on 31 October 2019
whatChanged: NCRB's custodial-death universe is police custody and lockup only. Chapter 16A of Crime in India is titled 'Custodial Crimes & Complaints Against Police Personnel', its 2022 Table 16A.6 is titled 'Cases Registered against State Police Personnel for Human Right Violation', and its bounding notes - identical across the 2019, 2020 and 2022 volumes - establish that the remand and non-remand split is a procedural split inside police custody rather than a police-versus-judicial one, and that the data are 'As per data provided by States/UTs' rather than NCRB's own observations. Table 16A.3 splits deaths across seven causes, of which the column corresponding to what most readers mean by a custodial death - 'Injuries sustained during the police custody due to physical assault by police' - registers two of 85 nationally in 2019 and one of 75 in 2022, against suicide and illness which dominate. And the J&K series breaks on 31 October 2019: J&K appears as a State in the Crime in India 2019 tables and as a UT thereafter with Ladakh split out, in both Chapter 16A and Prison Statistics India, so the post-2019 figure covers a smaller territory. Confirmed on the documents in phase 12, with two refinements. Thirteen full Prison Statistics India volumes were retrieved: J&K appears at Sl. No. 10 in the STATES block with zero occurrences of 'Ladakh' anywhere in the volume through PSI 2019, and at Sl. No. 33 in the UNION TERRITORIES block with Ladakh at Sl. No. 34 from PSI 2020. FIRST, the break is a property of the volume's single State/UT list and therefore governs EVERY table in the volume, not Table 8.1 alone - it reaches every J&K quantity anyone draws from PSI. SECOND, the break in the instrument is fourteen months later than the break in the referent: PSI 2019's reference date of 31 December 2019 is sixty-one days after J&K ceased to be a State, and that volume still reports a State of Jammu and Kashmir with Ladakh folded in and no footnote at the row.
when: 31 October 2019 for the territorial break; the structural bounding runs throughout
bridgeNote: No bridge across the territorial break, because Ladakh is separated out with no restated back-series for J&K on the new boundary. And no bridge to the missing population at all: there is no category, column, row or footnote anywhere in Chapter 16A for deaths in the custody of the Army, Rashtriya Rifles, CRPF, BSF or any other central armed police force, so a death in such custody in J&K has no cell to be recorded in. NCRB nowhere says it excludes armed-forces custody - it simply has no such category, and no stated reason may be attributed to it.

competingAccounts.position: Police and public order are State subjects, Crime in India is compiled from State and UT returns, and every row is a State or UT because that is who reports. Central armed police forces report through their own ministries and the Army through the Ministry of Defence, so a cell for them in a state-police compendium would have no reporting line to fill it. NCRB has never claimed the chapter is a complete national account of custodial death, and its own footnotes say so.

In the one theatre where central forces do most of the holding, no instrument counts the resulting deaths and no instrument could. The absence is silent rather than declared, so a reader meeting a J&K custodial-death figure has no way to know what it omits. And there is nowhere else for the count to go: section 19 of the Protection of Human Rights Act confines the NHRC, for complaints against the armed forces - defined to include any other armed forces of the Union, which pulls the CRPF and BSF in - to seeking a report from the Central Government and then dropping the matter or recommending, and the 24-hour custodial-death intimation regime is addressed only to District Magistrates and Superintendents of Police.

title: Local recruitment into militancy: mutually exclusive official claims, and a category defined by absence from the list
whatChanged: There is no series. Zero occurrences of a counted local-recruitment quantity in seventeen MHA Annual Reports and none in any parliamentary reply retrieved, while the subject appears as a policy aspiration in near-identical prose for over a decade. What circulates are police press-conference claims which conflict with one another: 2018 given as 187, as 218 and as over 200; 2019 as 119 or 140; 2020 as 130 to September, 184 for the year, and also 181; 2021 as 82 to July, 125 for the year, and also 142; 2022 as 100, 110 or 130; 2023 as 10 or 22; 2024 as 7 or fewer than 10. The variance is the finding: for 2022 the same authority is reported saying 100, 110 and 130, and for 2018 three official attributions give three answers. The pre-2018 figures - 66, 88 and 126 for 2015 to 2017 - exist because an MLA asked and a Chief Minister answered in writing in the J&K Assembly on 6 February 2018, and that route is closed. The instrument changed from an answer to a claim.
when: 2015 onward; the 'hybrid militant' category introduced October-November 2021
bridgeNote: No bridge, because there is no instrument to bridge to. No published definition of recruitment was found from any body: confirmed joining, missing-with-weapon and intelligence estimate are different quantities and no source distinguishes them. The direction of travel - a large fall - is consistent across every version; the magnitude is not establishable to better than a wide band, and any point value entering an instrument would be laundering.

competingAccounts.position: Recruitment has collapsed and every corroborating indicator moves with it: militants killed fell from 257 in 2018 to 67 in 2024, infiltration attempts from 419 to 53 and net estimated infiltration from 136 to 14, and over 1,900 overground workers were detained between 2019 and 2023. The hybrid-militant category was not invented to hide recruits - it was coined to describe a real and novel adversary tactic adopted because conventional recruitment had become suicidal, and the police announced it publicly and repeatedly as their biggest challenge for 2022, which is not how an organisation behaves when concealing a category.

The numbers are announced at press conferences by the officer whose performance they measure, unpublished in any statistical return, absent from seventeen consecutive Annual Reports, and internally inconsistent by 30 to 120 per cent for the same year. There is no document to audit. And in the middle of the fall the same force introduced a category whose defining property, in its own words, is not appearing on the official list of militants - people who joined militancy without being counted as having joined it. Whether they are added back is a question nobody has answered, and nobody has been in a position to compel an answer since the assembly stopped sitting.

title: Identity is declared by the force that killed, and the error in the series runs one way
whatChanged: The categories 'Terrorists killed' and 'Civilians killed' are populated at the point of an encounter, by the force that conducted it, before independent identification, and since April 2020 the body is then buried in a remote graveyard rather than released to the family. No written order establishes that practice and on the police's own account none exists. The consequence for the series is demonstrable rather than inferential, on three retrieved instances. At Amshipora on 18 July 2020 three civilian labourers entered the record as unidentified hardcore terrorists and were buried 125 km away with no photographs released; absent three missing-person complaints filed 160 km away, MHA's 2020 figure of 221 militants killed would have contained three civilians permanently. The police protocol itself makes identification conditional on a family learning of the death, obtaining a lockdown travel pass, reaching Srinagar in time and being believed by two District Commissioners - four filters, each of which can fail without anyone recording that it failed. At Ganderbal in 2026 the dead man was identified only because papers happened to be on his body, and his family waited 75 days.
when: April 2020 onward for the burial practice; the classification mechanism runs throughout
bridgeNote: No bridge and, while the practice stands, none can be built. The rate of misclassification is not merely unbuilt but unbuildable from published material: the only instrument that could establish it - independent identification of the dead - is what the practice removes. What can be established is the direction. The error is structurally one-directional, from civilian into terrorist and not the reverse, because a body wrongly recorded as a militant is buried far away and unphotographed while a body wrongly recorded as a civilian would be claimed immediately.

competingAccounts.position: Against 731 operations and 1,142 militants killed between 2018 and 2024, the number of cases in which identity has been contested and subsequently established as wrong is very small, and Amshipora is named by everyone precisely because it is exceptional - and exceptional in a second way, because the state established it, opened the inquiry itself and court-martialled the officer. Safeguards exist and were stated with dated worked examples: post-mortem and DNA are taken, families may identify before a magistrate, and where identity is later established exhumation and handover follow.

The base-rate argument assumes the denominator is knowable and it is not. The check on the state's declaration is a family that hears in time, travels, is believed and gets DNA run, and Amshipora is a demonstration not that the system self-corrects but of what correcting it takes - three simultaneous complaints, sustained press attention and eleven weeks. The machinery for testing disputes does not function either: 506 magisterial inquiries since 1990, one completed, that report never submitted, no convictions - and that figure comes from an advocacy petition to the State Human Rights Commission rather than from a government return, and must be graded as a claimed figure.

title: The producer and the publisher of the J&K security figures became the same ministry, with no seam in the arithmetic
whatChanged: Before 31 October 2019 these figures were produced by a state police force answerable to a state Home Department under a Chief Minister answerable to a sitting legislature. On the appointed day under the J&K Reorganisation Act 2019, Police and Public Order ceased to be within the legislative competence of the J&K legislature and the police reporting line came to run to the Lieutenant Governor and thence to MHA. In the same window the statistics changed chapters and owners: J&K security figures sat in the Internal Security chapter alongside the Left Wing Extremism and North East series from at least the Annual Report 2008-09 to 2018-19, and from 2019-20 move to a dedicated territorial chapter under a Department of Jammu, Kashmir and Ladakh Affairs restructured and renamed in the same move. MHA's tables run continuously across 31 October 2019 with no seam of any kind. That is precisely why this is recorded: the instrument shows no discontinuity at the point where the independent check on it was removed.
when: 31 October 2019, the appointed day under the J&K Reorganisation Act 2019
bridgeNote: No arithmetic bridge is needed and none should be drawn: this record exists as a provenance attachment to every J&K security series rather than as a seam in any one of them, because a seam would assert an arithmetic discontinuity that is not established. Whether the underlying collection instrument at police-station level changed at reorganisation - whether the pipeline that produces terrorist-initiated incidents was altered - could not be established. The continuity of the tables is consistent both with no change and with a change absorbed silently, and no document was found either way.

competingAccounts.holder: The case that nothing measurable changed
competingAccounts.position: The tables are continuous across the date and no restatement accompanies it, which is what one would expect if the returns pipeline was unaffected. Every reorganisation of a territory changes reporting lines without changing what is counted, and the reallocation of Police and Public Order is a constitutional consequence rather than a measurement decision.

competingAccounts.holder: The case that answerability is part of the measurement
competingAccounts.position: A figure produced by a force answerable to a legislature that can compel written answers and a figure produced by a force answerable only to the ministry that publishes it are not the same kind of fact, even where the arithmetic is identical. The producer and the consumer of the numbers became the same ministry, the figures moved out of the chapter where they sat beside comparable internal-security series, and a comparison of J&K against Left Wing Extremism or the North East across 2019 is a comparison across a change in producing unit.
